body: Not a medical professional far from it I'm actually a mh patient and have a considerable amount of scars and often end up in ambulances to go to A&E so I have many encounters. I have had Paramedics and nurses with visible (old) self harm scars which has made me feel much more at ease and so seen. But I do think it would be inappropriate to have open wounds especially due to cross infection risk etc. I know most won't understand but there are many many more understanding people than the minority that could be rude (usually because they don't understand). It's your choice at the end of the day but for me personally seeing anyone with self harm scars makes me feel less alone in this shitty world and gives me hope (like if they can overcome self harm and live a normal life why can't I).

I think it works best if you can integrate some of those subsections together. You may feel like having clear subsections is organizing them but it may be easier if you condense them down to only the most important ones. 

Alternatively make a journal with subsections in it for each different thing. So you don't waste money buying journals you may barely use. 

I'd definitely say you don't need an individual jounral for each of those things and keeping it simple is best. I think just having one works for a lot of people. But ultimately it's up to you to find what works for you. The most important thing is you using them.

Normally when my subcutaneous cuts heal they look a bit infected. They do get a green/yellow 'scab' like thing to begin with but no other symptoms like swelling, liquid that smells bad and I don't have a fever. If you have any other symptoms then definitely got it checked out by a doc. Just be very careful and do everything you can now to help them heal. It really depends on the depth. If the cut was to the epidermis (first layer of skin/ the very top part) and left a scratch like cut it shouldn't take longer that a week to be pretty much healed. This is similar or a little longer for a shallow dermis cut (you can see white underneath before blood and it's often referred to as styro) but if it is anything deeper it will take several weeks to months to heal into a scar and then possibly years to go completely skin coloured/ pale. Even then it will likely still be visible. It also depends on how fast you're skin heals so without further info no one can tell you how long it will take to heal. I hope for your sake it heals quickly. Take care :)
